facts.fact: Togo First reports that Michel Yaovi Galley, head of Togo's regulator ARCEP, was elected president of the West Africa Telecommunications Regulators Assembly (WATRA) in April 2026 at its 23rd General Assembly in Lomé.

Tech Review Africa reports that the regulators of Senegal (ARTP), Togo (ARCEP Togo) and Benin (ARCEP Benin) signed agreements for a free roaming arrangement between the three countries, launched in Lomé on 24 April 2026 under ECOWAS regulation C/REG.21/12/17; the signing date is not given, so the launch date is used.

Tech Review Africa reports the free roaming arrangement between Senegal, Togo and Benin took effect on 24 April 2026 in Lomé, with free incoming calls for up to 30 consecutive days and no surcharge on incoming international traffic.

Togo First reports that ARCEP Togo hosted the 23rd annual General Assembly of the West Africa Telecommunications Regulators Assembly (ARTAO/WATRA) in Lomé, with the inaugural ceremony set for 22 April 2026 and round tables held two days earlier.

note: Only a bilateral ministers' meeting in Lomé on digital collaboration; talks opened, no agreement signed and no African body named.

facts.fact: The ATU reports that the country is among 23 states that have endorsed the 49 African Common Proposals for the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference 2026.

facts.fact: Smart Africa names Togo among the 19 signatories of the SATA Declaration on digital trust and cross-border interoperability.
Ecofin Agency reports on 26 October 2026 that the Benin-Togo roaming agreement took effect on 1 January 2024, and Benin, Senegal and Togo launched roaming among themselves in April 2026.
Ecofin Agency reports on 26 October 2026 that Mali reached roaming agreements with Benin and Togo in December 2023.
